info.title: Org Service
info.description:
# Overview
The Organizer Service allows managing hierarchical breakdown structures. Each breakdown structure is represented as a tree. Trees are organized in forests, a group of trees. Typically forests would be mapped to projects. Each tree consists of nodes. Nodes are managed as a flat list but clients are expected to organize them into the tree kind of structure based on common name prefixes. Each node has a set of links associated with it. Links are opaque strings that are expected to be interpreted by clients.

Documentation for this service is available on the [Trimble Developer](https://developer.trimble.com/docs/connect/organizer) site.

# Getting started
**You must agree to the [Terms of Service](https://developer.trimble.com/docs/connect/terms) to use Connect services.**

You need to complete the steps in the [Getting started](https://developer.trimble.com/docs/connect/getting_started) guide to be able to call the API.

# Concepts
Please see [Common Concepts](https://developer.trimble.com/docs/connect#common-concepts) in the Connect Platform documentation.

## Change notifications
The Subscribe API allows getting url for creating a WebSocket connection to the service.
A standard WebSocket API may be used, no additional library is needed.A webSocket connection
may be used to receive notification messages of changes on any resource the user has access to.
Notifications are delivered at best effort, in some rare cases, notifications can be lost.
A periodic full refresh of the local cache is recommended.

A Notification WebSocket is opened using the credentials of the subscribing user. Change notifications will be published
for every change in each resource managed by the service if and only if the user has read access
(org:GetXXX action) to the changed resource.

After opening the WebSocket connection, the client needs to send a subscription message to start receiving change notification messages. Before that, the subscription service will send only keepalive messages.
```json
{
  "type": "Subscribe"
}
```

The notification message has type "Data". The Notification message payload has the same syntax as BatchGetRequest, in other words, it contains objects with arrays of resource identifiers.
The resource version is always included in the identifier.
```json
{
  "type": "Data",
  "payload":  { "trees":
    [
      {
        "forestId" : "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
        "treeId" : "yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy",
        "v" : 2
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
```json
{
  "type": "Data",
  "payload":  { "nodes":
    [
      {
        "forestId" : "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
        "treeId" : "yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy",
        "nodeId" : "zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz"
        "v" : 9
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The service sends periodic keepalive messages to all connected clients (type "Ka", no payload). No reply from the client is expected. In other words, the client can silently ignore these messages. Also, the client can send keepalive messages. The service will not reply to them.
```json
{
  "type": "Ka"
}
```

## Deprecated Change notifications
The set of `Subscribe` APIs allows subscribing to the change notifications in different scopes (forest, tree, node).
The notifications are delivered with MQTT protocol over HTTP.
To consume notifications in browser-based apps you can use https://www.npmjs.com/package/cdm-notify-client as a convenient wrapper for the AWS IoT Device class.
The payload of each change notification is a JSON object with a `location` property that identifies the changed resource as a relative URL 
and the `v` property that informs the new version of the changed resource.

Note that notification topic names should not be parsed to get the resource identity as they might be scrambled.

## Eventual Read Consistency
The service internally stores data in several Availability Zones within a Region. Each Availability Zone is isolated from failures in other Availability Zones and provides inexpensive, low-latency network connectivity to other Availability Zones in the same Region. This allows rapid replication of your data among multiple Availability Zones in a Region.

When your application writes data to the service and receives an HTTP 200 response (OK), the write has occurred and is durable. The data is eventually consistent across all storage locations, usually within a second.

When you read data from the service, the response might not reflect the results of a recently completed write operation. The response might include some stale data. If you repeat your read request after a short time, the response will return the latest data.

## Resource Identifiers
The client is allowed to assign an identifier (id) to the resource when they are created.
This is often used to correlate different resources by id. For example, you can have a forest with the same identifier as a project to indicate this is a project level forest. This way a forest can be found just by id lookup when the user opens a project.
If the client does not pass the id in the request the id will be generated and assigned automatically and returned in the response.
You can use any UTF-8 character in an object key name, except the slash ('/'). However, using certain characters in key names may cause problems with some applications and protocols.
If the identifier contains characters that are not url safe they must be urlencoded when used in the URLs (but not in the request and response bodies).

## Names
Tree and node names are optional. Usually, an application enforces on the UI level that the user must enter a name.
If a node or tree is used to store system information that is not presented to the user directly the name is usually not needed.

The service does not enforce the uniqueness of the names, for example, for nodes in the same tree or trees in the same forest.
If this is needed, the uniqueness of the names should be enforced on the application level. In any case, the application should be prepared to handle nonunique names and to allow the users to correct the situation.

## Tree type
The tree type is a required attribute that indicates the semantics of the tree and behavior attached to the tree.
Currently, on the service level, there are no special behaviors attached to tree types, but the service enforces that a type must be defined on the tree creation and does not allow changes to the type later.

## Links
Links are pointers to external resources. The service does not interpret the content or links in any way.

It is recommended to use the [FRN notation](https://drive.google.com/open?id=1gR1PEhrR58WGlrZt8PPWqTPbjvbEwXVK) for links.

A small number of links are stored and transferred inline with the node descriptor.
But if the size of the linkset is big the service automatically uses external storage for the links and will not inline the linkset into the node descriptor responses.
Instead, the service will pass a time-limited (5 minutes) URL that the client can use to download the linkset.
This can be used for performance optimizations, for example, an application can list all nodes in a tree and then load linksets for all nodes in parallel.
Externalized linksets are stored in the JSON array format (application/json) where each link is a separate element of the array.

When node descriptor is returned
1. If the `nolinks` parameter is not specified. The node descriptor will have `links` or `linksUrl` property.
2. If the `nolinks` parameter is given in the request. The node descriptor will have `linksUrl` or both `links` and `linksUrl` properties will be missing.
In the latter case, it means that links are inlined and the node descriptor should be requested without the `nolinks` query parameter.

### Representing a hierarchy of nodes
The service keeps a linear list of nodes for each tree for scalability reasons.
Hierarchy is mostly a presentation-level concept. To encode a hierarchy of nodes a naming convention should be used (similar to AWS S3).
Hierarchical segments in the node name must use the `/` (forward slash) character as a separator. 
The node with the name that ends on `/` might be treated as a virtual/folder type of node depending on the application.
When presenting a node as a hierarchy, the application must be prepared to intermediate levels of virtual nodes on the fly,
since service does not guarantee that all levels will be present on a persistent level.

The service supports some special operations (like listing) that take the node name prefix into consideration to help with working with subtrees. This includes setting of permissions to subtrees.

## Versioning and History
Versioning and concurrency are implemented on a resource level (the node).
Each time a resource is modified its version is incremented automatically (starting from zero).

Data is never really deleted but only marked as deleted/inactive. Marking resources as deleted creates a new version of the resource.
A resource that is marked as deleted still can be accessed by a specific version number or by specifying the `deleted` query parameter. If the `deleted` query parameter is not specified when requesting the current version of a resouce, a 404 error response is returned.
The resource can be undeleted by modifying it.

Most APIs that apply changes to resources (POST, PATCH, DELETE) support the `If-Match` header to implement conditional updates. In this way, API users can ensure changes are being done to the latest version of the resource.
The value of the `If-Match` header must match the ETag value returned on the resource creation or from GET request.

## Access Control
Access Control (AC) is done through policies on a tree level.
The policy describes who can do what with the tree descriptor and nodes in this tree.

Access control for individual nodes is not supported.
Access Control on a global level is not supported. Any authenticated user can create a tree.

The policy document is a JSON-formatted set of statements. Each statement is a tuple of effect, principal, resource, and action.

```json
{
  "id": string, // an optional identifier of the policy document
  "version": "2020-04-06", // policy document version (default `unnamed`)
  "statements": [
    {
      "id": string, an optional statement ID; allows differentiating between specific statements,
      "effect": string, allowed values are 'Allow' or 'Deny',
      "principal": // principals the statement applicable to, string or array of strings can be used as a short form
      {
        "any": [...],
        "all": [...],
        "notAny": [...],
        "notAll": [...]
      },
      "action": // actions the statement applicable to, string or array of strings can be used as a short form
      {
        "any": [...],
        "all": [...],
        "notAny": [...],
        "notAll": [...]
      },
      "resource": // resources the statement applicable to, string or array of strings can be used as a short form
      {
        "any": [...],
        "all": [...],
        "notAny": [...],
        "notAll": [...]
      },
      "conditions": // conditions allows you to write access rules that are evaluated against the actual state of the resource that is accessed as an object in a JsonLogic format.
      Please see https://jsonlogic.com/ for more details. (Optional attribute)
    },
    ...
  ]
}
```

### Policy document versioning
Currently, two versions of the policy document are supported:

- `unnamed`
- `2020-04-06`

The version of the policy document must be given using the `version` property.
All clients must check the version of the policy document before parsing it and handle the situations gracefully in case they don't know the version of the policy returned.

If the `version` property is missing the version is assumed `unnamed`. Otherwise the value of this property must be `2020-04-06`.

The version of the policy document defines a supported schema and capabilities of the AC policy.
The difference between the policy versions is

* the `unnamed` policy supports only string and an array of string values for the `principal`, `action`, and `resource` properties.
* the `2020-04-06` policy introduces the object value type for `principal`, `action` and `resource` properties with logical operators (`all`, `any`, `notAny`, `notAll`), it adds a capability to express more complex logical conditions in the policy.

### Logical operators
When evaluating the statement, `principal`, `action`, and `resource` properties are checked and all of them must match the request context for the statement to be applied.
Each `principal`, `action`, and `resource` statement property may be defined as a combination of four possible logical operators:

* `any`
* `all`
* `notAny`
* `notAll`

All operators are optional, but at least one operator must be present. Operator, if present, cannot be empty.
Between operators, the AND logic is used. The meaning of each operator is defined below.

```
any: [a, b, c] => (a OR b OR c)
all: [a, b, c] => (a AND b AND c)
notAny: [a, b, c] => !(a OR b OR c)
notAll: [a, b, c] => !(a AND b AND c)
```
For any of the `principal`, `action`, and `resource`, a shortcut syntax may also be used:
* If the value of the property is an array, the value translates to the `any` operator, for example, `"principal": ["sub:<id1>", "sub:<id2>"]`
* If the value of the property is a string, the value translates to the `any` operator with a single element in the array, for example, `"principal": "sub:<id1>"`

The following example shows using the operators in a statement that allows viewer access for all users in the project "LLtnGeN6FV4" that do not belong to groups "cUsPU6NJc6A" or "122" - a kind of default access level for all users expect for predefined groups of people.

```json
{
  "id": "ViewerLevel",
  "effect": "Allow",
  "principal": {
      "any": ["project:LLtnGeN6FV4"],
      "notAny": ["group:cUsPU6NJc6A", "group:122"]
  },
  "action": ["pset:Get*", "pset:List*", "pset:Subscribe"],
  "resource": "*"
}
```

The negative `notAny` and `notAll` operators are not recommended to be used without `any` or `all` operators in the `Allow` statements, as this could easily cause unintentionally wide information exposure.
The negative operators can be used in `Deny` statements to strongly deny some actions for other that specific group of principals, for example, if the user does not have an ADMIN role they must be denied the action on a resource.

### Principal claims
To identify a principal, the following expressions may be used:

* `user:<id>` - a specific user by Trimble ID identifier (Legacy prefix. For all new requests should be used "sub:")
* `sub:<id>` - a specific user or application by Trimble ID identifier
* `azp:<id>` - a specific authorized party by Trimble ID identifier
* `email:<email>` - specific user by the verified primary email
* `domain:<email_domain>` - any user who's verified primary email is from the given domain
* `project:<id>[:<role>]` - member of the project with given identifier and optional role. Known roles are 'USER', 'ADMIN'. If the role is not specified then a member with any role matches.
* [DEPRECATED] `company:<id>[:<role>]` - member of the company with given identifier and optional role. Known roles are 'USER', 'ADMIN'. If the role is not specified then a member with any role matches.
* `group:<id>` - a member of the group with the given identifier.
* `role:<role>` - the user with given role. Known roles are 'SITE_ADMIN'
* `account:<id>` - the user who is a member of an account with a given id.
* `accountAdmin:<id>` - the user who is an administrator of an account with a given id. Note that the account administrator might be not a member of the account.
* `*` - the asterisk wildcard is used as a placeholder for any authenticated user

You can also specify more than one principal with an array using any combination of the methods previously shown. In this case, the statement will apply to the principal that matches any of the listed conditions.

The following example matches the user with the SITE_ADMIN role or member of the project 12312489 or ADMIN member of the company 898687.

```
"principal": [
    "role:SITE_ADMIN",
    "project:12312489",
    "company:898687:ADMIN"
  ]
```

### Action
Access control is fine-grained. There is an action for almost every individual API request
with the exception of batch APIs that apply access control internally to every executed action inside the batch.

Access Control on a forest level is not supported. Any authenticated user can create a tree in any forest.

The following actions are supported:

* `org:CreateTree` - not supported at the moment. Any authenticated user is allowed to create a new tree
* `org:ListTrees` - not supported at the moment. No such API.
* `org:GetTree`
* `org:UpdateTree`
* `org:GetTreePolicy`
* `org:UpdateTreePolicy`
* `org:GetNode`
* `org:CreateNode`
* `org:UpdateNode` - action that allows any changes in the node including links.
* `org:UpdateNodeLinks` - action that allows to update only links property of the node, but e.g. does not allow to rename a node.
* `org:ListNodes`
* `org:GetNodeVersions`
* `org:GetNodeVersion`
* `org:Subscribe`
* The `*` is a wildcard that indicates any action

The `*` (asterisk) is supported as a wildcard suffix for actions, for example, `org:GetNode*` would refer to all actions that start from `org:GetNode`.
Actions are named to allow convenient grouping using a prefix for common access control patterns.

An empty array of actions is also supported. Statements with an empty action array do not grant or revoke
any action for the principal and resource. In other words, these kind of arrays may be considered a documental statement.

An empty array of actions is supported only in shortcut format, not with operators.
```
  "action": [],
```

### Resources
:exclamation: WARNING, THIS WILL CHANGE!
Resources are identified by name with `*` and a wildcard suffix. The `*` corresponds to any resource.
E.g. the `root/*` corresponds to any node with a name that starts with `root/`. This notation allows defining access to subtrees.

### Conditions
This is an optional attribute.

Conditions provide a possibility to write access rules that are evaluated against the actual state of the resource that is accessed.

Notice that the evaluation of conditions will only occur if all previous evaluation steps was been successful.

Use the "var" JsonLogic operator to refer to claims or the resource that is accessed.

`{ "var": "node.metadata.prop1 "}`

During the evaluation, this expression will be replaced by the value of prop1 of the node.
Notice that if the referred resource or resource property was not found, the result of the condition logic will be false.

Supported var prefixes:
* "claims" - used to refer to the user or application claims.

claims keys
* `sub` - a specific user or application by Trimble ID identifier.
* `identity_type` - a type of identity `application` or  `user`.
* `azp` - a specific authorized party by Trimble ID identifier.
* `email` - a specific user by the verified primary email.
* `prj` - member of the project with given identifier.
* `prjrole` -  member of the project with given identifier and role. Known roles are 'USER', 'ADMIN'. Syntax: <project id>:<role>.
* [DEPRECATED] `cmpn` - member of the company with given identifier and optional role. Known roles are 'USER', 'ADMIN'.
* `grp`- a member of the group with the given identifier..
* `role` - the user with given role. Known roles are 'SITE_ADMIN'.
* `acc` - the user who is a member of an account with a given id..
* `accadm` - the user who is an administrator of an account with a given id. Note that the account administrator might be not a member of the account.

* "node" - used to refer to the state of node that is accessed.

Notice that org:ListNodes action will be validated against the tree. And org:GetNode will be validated against the node instance.
Ensure to add org:ListNodes allowed statement. Please see AC Policy Examples: Allow org:ListNodes action only if node metadata public property equals true.

### AC Policy Evaluation Logic
After the user is authenticated (with Trimble ID), the service processes the request context to gather the policies that need to be evaluated. Based on gathered policies a decision is made whether the request is allowed or denied using the logic outlined below.

When a principal sends a request, the enforcement code decides whether a given request should be allowed or denied. The following is a high-level summary of the evaluation logic

1. By default, all requests are denied. (Except new tree creation requests are allowed for any authenticated user). The initial decision assumption is "deny".
2. An explicit deny in any policy statement overrides any allows (for example, coming from the permission boundary assigned to the user), and leads to an immediate deny decision.
3. (This step is not supported yet) If there is a permissions boundary defined (by for example, a central auth and/or licensing service), this boundary (if it exists), must explicitly allow the action. Otherwise, it is implicitly denied.
4. If there is an allow in any policy statement -> allow, otherwise -> deny.

### Default AC Policy
When a new tree is created, a default access control policy is attached automatically if not explicitly provided in the creation request.
Best practices are to always provide an AC policy explicitly when creating a resource.

The default access control policy grants full access to the tree and nodes in this tree to the creator only.

```json
{
  "version": "2020-04-06",
  "statements": [
    {
      "id": "creator",
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "sub:<id>",
      "action": "*",
      "resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Context actions and effective permissions
To help applications to build intelligent UIs, effective caller permissions are returned together with resources in response bodies.
The effective permissions are returned in a form of a collection of context-specific actions that the caller can perform with the returned resource.

The `tree` resource context actions are:
* `org:GetTree`
* `org:GetTreePolicy`
* `org:UpdateTree`
* `org:UpdateTreePolicy`
* `org:ListNodes`
* `org:Subscribe`
* `org:CreateNode`

This set also includes actions to create a child resource.

The `node` resource context actions are:
* `org:GetNode`
* `org:GetNodeVersion`
* `org:GetNodeVersions`
* `org:UpdateNode`
* `org:UpdateNodeLinks`
* `org:Subscribe`

The collection of context actions is returned in the `_actions` metadata property of the response.
This property is metadata that does not belong to the resource state and should be treated as volatile information not related to the resource version.
If action is present in the `_actions`, the current caller is likely allowed to execute this action on the resource, if action is missing, then the caller does not have a corresponding right.

:exclamation: WARNING :exclamation:
The information about effective permissions is volatile, it might change any moment between fetching the resource and executing the action. So the `_actions` metadata property should be treated as informational only, not as a promise.
For mutation actions (`org:Create*` and `org:Update*`) the effective permission cannot be calculated precisely in advance because the access control decision for mutation actions depends on the submitted state of the resource.
The returned effective permissions for the mutation actions is for the optimistic case, indicating if there is any possibility that a new resource state could allow the action.
So it might be that the mutation action would fail even if metadata indicates that this action is allowed.

### AC Policy Examples
Allow everything to a user - in this case the, creator, Jane Doe.

```json
{
  "version": "2020-04-06",
  "statements": [
    {
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "sub:a063104d-b92d-445f-91e4-6f75c724d2a2",
      "action": "*",
      "resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

Company private tree

```json
{
  "version": "2020-04-06",
  "statements": [
    {
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "domain:tekla.com",
      "action": "*",
      "resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

Company public tree.
All users from the "tekla.com" company can read and write. All users from companies other than "tekla.com" have read-only access.

```json
{
  "version": "2020-04-06",
  "statements": [
    {
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "domain:tekla.com",
      "action": "*",
      "resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "*",
      "action": ["org:GetTree","org:ListNodes", "org:GetNode*"],
      "resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

Personal tree.
Only a specific user can modify the tree. All others can read.

```json
{
  "version": "2020-04-06",
  "statements": [
    {
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "sub:a063104d-b92d-445f-91e4-6f75c724d2a2",
      "action": "*",
      "resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "*",
      "action": ["org:GetTree","org:ListNodes", "org:GetNode*"],
      "resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

Company public tree plus allow other companies (for example, a subcontractor) to edit a subtree.

```json
{
  "version": "2020-04-06",
  "statements": [
    {
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "domain:tekla.com",
      "action": "*",
      "resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "domain:google.com",
      "action": "*",
      "resource": "site/building/floor/*"
    },
    {
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "*",
      "action": ["org:GetTree","org:ListNodes", "org:GetNode*"],
      "resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

Other project members.
All project members that are NOT members of given user groups have default read-only access.

```json
{
  "version": "2020-04-06",
  "statements": [
    {
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": {
        "any: "project:1",
        "notAny: ["group:1","group:2","group:3"],
      },
      "action": ["org:List*","org:Get*","org:Subscribe"],
      "resource": "*"
    },
  ]
}
```

Conditions.
Allow this actions only if node metadata public property equals true.

```json
{
  "version": "2020-04-06",
  "statements": [
    {
      "id": "id1",
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "*",
      "action": [
          "org:GetNode",
          "org:GetNodeVersion",
          "org:CreateNode",
          "org:UpdateNode"
      ],
      "resource": [
        "*"
      ],
      "conditions": {
        "===": [
          { "var": "node.metadata.public"},
          true
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Allow these actions only if node metadata public property is true or subject is the creator of this node.

```json
{
  "version": "2020-04-06",
  "statements": [
    {
    	"id": "id1",
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "*",
      "action": [
          "org:GetNode",
          "org:GetNodeVersion",
          "org:CreateNode",
          "org:UpdateNode"
      ],
      "resource": [
        "*"
      ],
      "conditions": {
        "or": [
          { "===": [
              { "var": "claims.sub" },
              { "var": "node.createdBy" }
          ]},
          { "===": [
              { "var": "node.metadata.public"},
              true
          ]}
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Allow org:ListNodes action only if node metadata public property equals true.

```json
{
  "version": "2020-04-06",
  "statements": [
    {
      "id": "id1",
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "*",
      "action": [
          org:ListNodes
      ],
      "resource": [
        "*"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "id2",
      "effect": "Allow",
      "principal": "*",
      "action": [
          "org:GetNode"
      ],
      "resource": [
        "*"
      ],
      "conditions": {
        "===": [
          { "var": "node.metadata.public"},
          true
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## (Experimental) How to improve performance by avoiding CORS pre-flight requests
Since Trimble Connect APIs are public, the CORS mechanism with pre-flight requests are not adding additional security.
You can improve the performance of your web app by using the following technique (all browsers supported except IE6/7 as they don't have `postMessage`)

On your web page add the following script.
It's important to include XDomain before any other library.
When XDomain loads, XHook replaces the current window.XMLHttpRequest.
So if another library saves a reference to the original window.XMLHttpRequest and uses that, XHook won't be able to intercept those requests.

```javascript
<script src="https://unpkg.com/xdomain@0.8.2/dist/xdomain.min.js" slave="https://org-api.connect.trimble.com/v1/proxy.html"></script>
```

Or if you are using multiple services use the following construct to add several slaves

```javascript
<script src="https://unpkg.com/xdomain@0.8.2/dist/xdomain.min.js"></script>
<script>
  xdomain.slaves({
    "https://pset-api.connect.trimble.com": "/v1/proxy.html",
    "https://org-api.connect.trimble.com": "/v1/proxy.html",
  });
</script>
```

After that, any XHR to https://org-api.connect.trimble.com origin mentioned in the `slave` property will automatically work without a pre-flight request

```javascript
// do some vanilla XHR
var xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
xhr.open("GET", "https://org-api.connect.trimble.com/v1/me");
xhr.onreadystatechange = function(e) {
  if (xhr.readyState === 4) console.log("got result ", xhr.responseText);
}
xhr.send();
```
